subject: MATH
title: Math 2
description: Second-grade mathematics aligned to the California Common Core: fluency with addition and subtraction facts within 20, place value to 1,000, adding and subtracting within 100 and 1,000 with place-value strategies, measuring length in standard units, money and time, picture graphs, bar graphs and line plots, arrays and odd/even numbers as a foundation for multiplication, and shapes and equal shares. Lessons follow a concrete–pictorial–abstract path with base-ten blocks, number lines, and real objects, and every week includes word problems, a fact-fluency routine, and a Friday check.
framework: California Common Core State Standards for Mathematics; 2023 California Mathematics Framework

standards.2.OA.A.1: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems (adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, comparing) with unknowns in all positions.
standards.2.OA.B.2: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies; by end of grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.
standards.2.OA.C.3: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members; write an even number as a sum of two equal addends.
standards.2.OA.C.4: Use addition to find the total number of objects in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and 5 columns; write an equation of equal addends.
standards.2.NBT.A.1: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent hundreds, tens, and ones; 100 is a bundle of ten tens.
standards.2.NBT.A.3: Read and write numbers to 1000 using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.
standards.2.NBT.A.4: Compare two three-digit numbers based on hundreds, tens, and ones digits using >, =, and <.
standards.2.NBT.B.5: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
standards.2.NBT.B.6: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
standards.2.NBT.B.7: Add and subtract within 1000 using concrete models, drawings, and place-value strategies; understand composing and decomposing tens and hundreds.
standards.2.NBT.B.8: Mentally add 10 or 100 to, and subtract 10 or 100 from, a number 100–900.
standards.2.NBT.B.9: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and properties of operations.
standards.2.MD.A.1: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools (rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, measuring tapes).
standards.2.MD.A.2: Measure the length of an object twice using different length units and describe how the measurements relate to the size of the unit.
standards.2.MD.A.3: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.
standards.2.MD.A.4: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the difference in a standard length unit.
standards.2.MD.B.5: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths given in the same units.
standards.2.MD.B.6: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram and represent sums and differences within 100 on a number line.
standards.2.MD.C.7: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.
standards.2.MD.C.8: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately.
standards.2.MD.D.9: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths to the nearest whole unit and show the data on a line plot.
standards.2.MD.D.10: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (single-unit scale) for a data set with up to four categories; solve put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using the graph.
standards.2.G.A.1: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes (number of angles or equal faces); identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.
standards.2.G.A.2: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.
standards.2.G.A.3: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares as halves, thirds, fourths, and recognize equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

units.title: Addition and Subtraction Fluency Within 20
units.big_idea: Facts within 20 can be found quickly with strategies like making ten, doubles, and thinking addition for subtraction.

units.title: Place Value to 1,000
units.big_idea: Three-digit numbers are made of hundreds, tens, and ones, and place value lets us read, write, and compare them.

units.title: Measuring Length
units.big_idea: We measure length by repeating equal units with no gaps, and smaller units give larger numbers.

units.title: Adding and Subtracting Within 100
units.big_idea: Place value lets us add and subtract two-digit numbers by combining or breaking apart tens and ones.

units.title: Data: Graphs and Line Plots
units.big_idea: Graphs organize data so we can compare categories and answer questions.

units.title: Adding and Subtracting Within 1,000
units.big_idea: The same place-value strategies work for hundreds: compose and decompose tens and hundreds as needed.

units.title: Money and Time
units.big_idea: Coins and bills have values we can count and combine; clocks show time in five-minute intervals.

units.title: Length Word Problems and Number Lines
units.big_idea: A number line is a ruler for numbers, and it helps solve length problems.

units.title: Equal Groups, Arrays, Odd and Even
units.big_idea: Equal groups and arrays prepare us for multiplication; even numbers can be split into two equal groups.

units.title: Geometry and Equal Shares
units.big_idea: Shapes are defined by their attributes, and wholes can be cut into equal shares called halves, thirds, and fourths.

units.title: Putting It All Together
units.big_idea: Mathematicians choose strategies and tools to solve multi-step problems and explain their thinking.

days.title: Number talk & ten-frames
days.work: Use quick-image dot cards and ten-frames to name numbers 1–10 and the 'partners of 10' (7 and 3, 6 and 4); write all ten facts that make 10.

days.title: Count on
days.work: Add 1, 2, or 3 by counting on from the larger addend (8 + 3: 9, 10, 11); play 'Roll and Count On' with two dice and record 15 equations.

days.title: Doubles
days.work: Learn doubles 1+1 to 10+10 with pictures (spider legs 4+4, egg carton 6+6) and quiz with flash cards.

days.title: Subtraction within 10
days.work: Act out take-away stories with counters and write subtraction equations; relate 9 − 4 to 4 + 5 = 9.

days.title: Fact check
days.work: Take a 2-minute baseline fact quiz (40 facts within 10) and graph your score to track all year. Solve 4 short add-to/take-from story problems.

weeks.assessment: Baseline fluency quiz and story problem check.

days.title: Make a ten
days.work: Solve 9 + 5 by moving one counter to make 10 + 4 on a double ten-frame; practice with 8 + and 9 + facts.

days.title: Near doubles
days.work: Use doubles to solve near doubles (6 + 7 = 6 + 6 + 1) and explain the strategy in words; sort 20 facts by best strategy.

days.title: Word problems
days.work: Solve 6 put-together/take-apart problems (e.g., 'Ana has 8 red and 7 blue marbles…') with a drawing and an equation.

days.title: Fact games
days.work: Play 'Make Ten Go Fish' and 'Doubles War' with cards; record 10 facts from each game.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on 30 addition facts within 20 and 3 word problems; explain one strategy aloud.

objectives: Subtract by counting back and through ten

days.title: Fact families
days.work: Build fact families with fact triangles (7, 8, 15) and write the 4 related equations for 6 families.

days.title: Think addition
days.work: Solve 14 − 6 by asking '6 + ? = 14'; practice 20 subtraction facts using the related addition fact.

days.title: Back through ten
days.work: Use a 0–20 number line to subtract through ten (15 − 7: back 5 to 10, back 2 more to 8).

days.title: Compare problems
days.work: Solve 'how many more/fewer' problems with bar models (e.g., 'Leo has 13 stickers, Mia has 8. How many more does Leo have?').

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Subtraction fact quiz (30 facts) and 4 mixed word problems with drawings and equations.

weeks.assessment: Subtraction fact quiz and mixed word problems.

weeks.topic: Unknowns in all positions and fluency check
objectives: Solve problems with unknown start or change

days.title: Missing addends
days.work: Solve equations with a box for the unknown (8 + □ = 15, □ − 4 = 9) using counters and a number line.

days.title: Start unknown
days.work: Solve 'Some birds were on a tree. 6 more came. Now there are 14. How many were there at first?' using bar models; solve 5 like it.

days.title: Write your own
days.work: Write 3 word problems (one with the unknown at the start, middle, end) for a family member to solve and check their answers.

days.title: Fluency stations
days.work: Rotate through fact games: fact-triangle flash, 'Salute!' card game, and an online fact practice session.

days.title: Unit 1 test
days.work: Fluency quiz (40 facts within 20, compare to Week 1 baseline) and 6 one-step word problems with unknowns in different positions.

weeks.assessment: Unit 1 test with fluency comparison to baseline.

objectives: Represent three-digit numbers with base-ten blocks
Identify the value of each digit

days.title: Bundling
days.work: Bundle straws into tens with rubber bands, then 10 tens into a hundred; explain why 100 = 10 tens.

days.title: Build numbers
days.work: Build 10 three-digit numbers on a place-value mat with base-ten blocks (e.g., 346 = 3 hundreds, 4 tens, 6 ones) and draw quick pictures.

days.title: Zeros matter
days.work: Build and compare 305, 350, and 503; explain what the zero means in each.

days.title: Hundreds
days.work: Count 100, 200, …, 900 with flats; show that 4 hundreds = 40 tens = 400 ones.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: write the number shown by 8 block pictures and give the value of the underlined digit in 8 numbers.

weeks.assessment: Place-value quiz on block pictures and digit values.

objectives: Find patterns on a hundreds chart

days.title: Counting across hundreds
days.work: Count aloud from 87 to 132 and from 385 to 421, filling a blank chart section; notice what happens at 'hundreds.'

days.title: Skip by 5s and 10s
days.work: Skip-count by 5s using nickels and by 10s using dimes; skip-count by 10s starting at 23 (23, 33, 43…).

days.title: Skip by 100s
days.work: Skip-count by 100s from 100 and from 250; use a number path to show 10 more, 10 less, 100 more, 100 less.

days.title: Mental 10s and 100s
days.work: Mental math: add or subtract 10 or 100 from numbers between 100 and 900 (e.g., 456 + 100, 702 − 10) — 20 problems.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Fill in missing numbers on 6 skip-count patterns and 10 '10 more/100 less' problems.

weeks.assessment: Skip-counting patterns and mental 10/100 more or less check.

objectives: Write numbers in standard form, word form, and expanded form

days.title: Expanded form
days.work: Use place-value arrow cards to show 427 = 400 + 20 + 7 and write expanded form for 10 numbers.

days.title: Number words
days.work: Practice spelling number words (twenty, forty, hundred) and write 8 numbers in word form (six hundred thirty-two).

days.title: Many ways
days.work: Show 245 four ways: blocks, quick picture, expanded form, and as 24 tens 5 ones.

days.title: Number riddles
days.work: Solve riddles ('I have 3 hundreds, 0 tens, and 9 ones') and write 3 riddles for a family member.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Convert 12 numbers among standard, word, and expanded forms.

objectives: Compare three-digit numbers using place value

days.title: Compare with blocks
days.work: Build two numbers (452 and 425) with blocks and compare hundreds first, then tens; record with > or <.

days.title: Symbols
days.work: Compare 15 pairs of numbers with >, =, < and explain one comparison in words ('362 > 326 because 6 tens is more than 2 tens').

days.title: Order
days.work: Order sets of 4 numbers from least to greatest; compare city populations or heights of landmarks in feet.

days.title: Greatest number game
days.work: Draw 3 digit cards, make the greatest and least possible numbers, and compare with a partner — 10 rounds.

days.title: Unit 2 test
days.work: Test on place value, counting patterns, number forms, and comparing three-digit numbers (20 items).

objectives: Measure length with a ruler and yardstick
Understand units are equal with no gaps

days.title: Why units
days.work: Measure a book with paper clips leaving gaps and overlaps, then correctly; discuss why units must be the same size with no gaps.

days.title: Inches
days.work: Measure 10 household objects (pencil, spoon, shoe) to the nearest inch with a ruler starting at 0; record in a table.

days.title: Feet and yards
days.work: Measure a table, a door, and a room with a yardstick or tape; choose the best tool for each and explain.

days.title: Estimate first
days.work: Estimate then measure 8 objects in inches or feet; find how close each estimate was.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Measure 6 pictured objects to the nearest inch and choose the right unit/tool for 6 situations.

weeks.assessment: Measurement accuracy check and tool/unit choice quiz.

materials: meter stick or string cut to 1 meter

days.title: Centimeters
days.work: Measure 10 small objects to the nearest centimeter and record; use a fingertip as a 1-cm benchmark.

days.title: Meters
days.work: Measure the length of rooms and a hallway with a meter stick; estimate first using a giant step as about 1 meter.

days.title: Two units
days.work: Measure the same 5 objects in inches and centimeters and explain why there are more centimeters (smaller unit).

days.title: Benchmark estimates
days.work: Estimate 8 lengths in cm or m using benchmarks, then measure; color estimates that were within 5 cm.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: measure in cm, compare inch vs. cm results for 3 objects, and explain the unit-size relationship in a sentence.

weeks.assessment: Metric measuring quiz and written unit-size explanation.

objectives: Find how much longer one object is than another

days.title: How much longer
days.work: Measure two pencils and find how much longer one is by counting on from the shorter length.

days.title: Ribbon compare
days.work: Cut ribbons of different lengths, measure each in cm, and write 5 'how much longer' sentences.

days.title: Toy car race
days.work: Roll toy cars down a ramp, measure distances, and find the difference between the farthest and shortest rolls.

days.title: Family lengths
days.work: Measure family members' arm spans in inches and write compare sentences ('Dad's arm span is 14 inches longer than mine').

days.title: Unit 3 test
days.work: Measure objects in two unit systems, estimate lengths, and solve 4 'how much longer' problems.

objectives: Add two-digit numbers by combining tens and ones

days.title: Add tens and ones
days.work: Add 34 + 25 with blocks: combine tens (5 tens), then ones (9 ones); solve 10 problems without regrouping.

days.title: Hundreds chart jumps
days.work: Add 46 + 23 on a hundreds chart by jumping down 2 rows (tens) and right 3 (ones); explain why it works.

days.title: Open number line
days.work: Add 38 + 27 on an open number line (38 + 20 = 58, + 2 = 60, + 5 = 65) and solve 8 more.

days.title: Making a new ten
days.work: Add 47 + 36 with blocks, trading 10 ones for 1 ten; draw quick pictures for 8 problems that need regrouping.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Solve 12 two-digit addition problems using a chosen strategy and explain one in writing.

weeks.assessment: Addition quiz with written strategy explanation.

objectives: Subtract two-digit numbers with and without decomposing a ten

days.title: Subtract tens and ones
days.work: Subtract 68 − 25 with blocks and quick pictures; solve 10 problems without decomposing.

days.title: Break a ten
days.work: Subtract 52 − 17 by trading a ten for 10 ones; solve 8 problems with drawings.

days.title: Count up
days.work: Solve 83 − 48 by counting up on a number line (48 → 50 → 80 → 83 = 35) and compare to the take-away method.

days.title: Check with addition
days.work: Solve 10 subtraction problems and check each with addition; explain why addition checks subtraction.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz of 12 subtraction problems within 100 and one written explanation of a strategy.

objectives: Add three and four two-digit numbers
Use properties to make friendly numbers

days.title: Three addends
days.work: Add 23 + 15 + 17 by finding a friendly pair first (23 + 17 = 40); solve 8 problems.

days.title: Four addends
days.work: Add four two-digit numbers by adding tens, then ones (24 + 31 + 12 + 18); use blocks to check.

days.title: Order doesn't matter
days.work: Show that 35 + 26 + 15 gives the same sum in any order and explain the property in your own words.

days.title: Shopping list
days.work: Add prices of 3–4 items from a grocery flyer (rounded to whole cents under $1, e.g., 45¢ + 29¢ + 18¢).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Solve 8 multi-addend problems and explain which numbers you grouped first and why.

weeks.topic: One- and two-step word problems within 100
objectives: Solve one- and two-step word problems
Use bar models and equations with unknowns

days.title: Bar models
days.work: Draw bar models for add-to, take-from, and compare problems within 100; solve 6 problems.

days.title: Two-step problems
days.work: Solve two-step problems ('There were 45 apples. 18 were sold, then 26 more were picked. How many now?') with labeled steps.

days.title: Unknown start
days.work: Solve problems where the start is unknown using bar models and related equations.

days.title: Reasonable?
days.work: Estimate answers to 6 problems before solving and decide if the final answers make sense.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Solve 6 mixed one- and two-step word problems showing a model and equation for each.

weeks.assessment: Word problem set with models and equations.

objectives: Choose efficient strategies for adding and subtracting within 100

days.title: Compensation
days.work: Solve 39 + 26 as 40 + 25 and 72 − 29 as 72 − 30 + 1; explain why changing numbers works.

days.title: Strategy choice
days.work: Sort 12 problems by best strategy (mental, number line, blocks, compensation) and solve them.

days.title: Target 100 game
days.work: Make two 2-digit numbers from cards whose sum is closest to 100; play 8 rounds and record equations.

days.title: Error analysis
days.work: Find and fix mistakes in 5 worked problems (e.g., forgot to regroup) and explain each error.

days.title: Unit 4 test
days.work: Add and subtract within 100 (16 items), add up to four two-digit numbers, and solve 3 two-step word problems.

objectives: Collect data with up to four categories
Draw picture graphs and bar graphs

days.title: Survey
days.work: Survey 10–20 family members, friends, or neighbors about their favorite fruit (4 choices) and record with tally marks.

days.title: Picture graph
days.work: Make a picture graph of the survey with a title, labels, and key (each picture = 1 vote).

days.title: Bar graph
days.work: Turn the same data into a bar graph with a single-unit scale and labeled axes.

days.title: Graph questions
days.work: Answer 'how many more/fewer' and 'how many in all' questions from 2 graphs and write 3 of your own.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Read a new bar graph and answer 6 put-together, take-apart, and compare questions.

weeks.assessment: Bar graph construction and graph-question quiz.

objectives: Make a line plot with whole-number units
materials: 15 pencils or crayons of different lengths

days.title: Measure a collection
days.work: Measure 15 pencils or crayons to the nearest inch and list the lengths.

days.title: Line plot
days.work: Draw a number line scale and place an X above each length to make a line plot; title and label it.

days.title: Hand spans
days.work: Measure hand spans of family members in centimeters and make a second line plot.

days.title: Interpret
days.work: Answer questions about the line plots: most common length, longest, shortest, and difference between them.

days.title: Unit 5 test
days.work: Make a line plot from given measurements and a bar graph from given data; answer 6 questions.

objectives: Add three-digit numbers with models and drawings

days.title: Add hundreds, tens, ones
days.work: Add 324 + 153 with blocks and quick pictures by place; solve 8 problems without regrouping.

days.title: Compose a ten
days.work: Add 247 + 136, trading 10 ones for a ten; record with quick pictures and partial sums.

days.title: Compose a hundred
days.work: Add 365 + 182, trading 10 tens for a hundred; explain the trade in words.

days.title: Partial sums
days.work: Use the partial-sums method (300 + 100, 60 + 80, 5 + 2) for 8 problems and match each to block drawings.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Solve 10 three-digit addition problems and explain one regrouping step.

days.title: Subtract by place
days.work: Subtract 586 − 243 with blocks; solve 8 problems without decomposing.

days.title: Decompose a ten
days.work: Subtract 462 − 128, breaking a ten into 10 ones; record with quick pictures.

days.title: Decompose a hundred
days.work: Subtract 531 − 274, breaking a hundred and a ten; explain each trade.

days.title: Zeros in the middle
days.work: Subtract across zeros (400 − 165, 302 − 147) using blocks and counting up; compare strategies.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Solve 10 subtraction problems within 1,000 and check 3 with addition.

objectives: Use number lines for three-digit numbers

days.title: 10 and 100 patterns
days.work: Use a 'number path' to show 10 more/less and 100 more/less for 10 numbers and describe which digit changes.

days.title: Number line jumps
days.work: Add 345 + 230 by jumping 200, then 30 on an open number line; solve 6 more.

days.title: Mental math race
days.work: Answer 30 quick '+10, −10, +100, −100' problems orally with a timer; record time.

days.title: Missing number puzzles
days.work: Solve chains like 472 → □ (+100) → □ (−10) → □ and create 2 puzzles.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: 15 mental math items and 4 number-line problems.

days.title: Story problems
days.work: Solve 5 story problems within 1,000 (e.g., 'A library had 425 books and got 138 more…') with drawings.

days.title: Estimate
days.work: Estimate sums and differences using nearest hundred before solving 6 problems.

days.title: Explain it
days.work: Write an explanation for how you solved 563 − 287, using place-value words.

days.title: Game: Race to 1,000
days.work: Roll dice to build 2-digit and 3-digit numbers and add until reaching 1,000 exactly; record equations.

days.title: Unit 6 test
days.work: Add and subtract within 1,000 (14 items), mental 10/100 items, and one written explanation.

days.title: Coin values
days.work: Sort real coins and learn values (1¢, 5¢, 10¢, 25¢); skip-count dimes by 10 and nickels by 5.

days.title: Count mixed coins
days.work: Count mixed coins starting with the greatest value (25, 35, 40, 41); count 10 handfuls and record.

days.title: Ways to make
days.work: Show 50¢ four different ways with coins and record with drawings.

days.title: Coin store
days.work: Run a pretend store with items under $1; pay with exact change and record each purchase.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Count 8 coin collections and solve 3 word problems with cents.

days.title: Dollars
days.work: Learn $1, $5, $10, $20 bills and count mixed bills; show that 100¢ = $1.

days.title: Money problems
days.work: Solve 6 problems like 'Jo has 2 dimes and 3 nickels. How many cents?' and 'Sam has $5 and $10 bills…'.

days.title: Making change
days.work: Pay $1 for items costing 65¢, 80¢, 42¢ and count up to find the change.

days.title: Budget challenge
days.work: Choose items from a pretend catalog under $20 total and show the addition.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Solve 8 money word problems using $ and ¢ correctly.

objectives: Tell time on analog and digital clocks to the nearest 5 minutes
Connect counting by 5s to the clock

days.title: Make a clock
days.work: Make a paper-plate clock with hands and label minutes by 5s around the edge.

days.title: Five-minute times
days.work: Read and show 12 times to the nearest 5 minutes (3:25, 7:50); match analog to digital.

days.title: a.m. and p.m.
days.work: Sort daily activities into a.m. or p.m. and make a schedule of your day with clock drawings.

days.title: Quarter and half past
days.work: Learn 'half past' and 'quarter past/to' language and tell the time on the house clock at 5 checkpoints today.

days.title: Unit 7 test
days.work: Tell and write 10 times, choose a.m. or p.m., and solve 6 money problems.

objectives: Represent numbers as lengths on a number line
Show sums and differences on a number line

days.title: Ruler to number line
days.work: Compare a measuring tape and a number line; make a 0–100 number line on adding-machine tape with tick marks every 5.

days.title: Show lengths
days.work: Mark numbers as lengths from 0 (e.g., 35) and show 35 + 20 and 35 − 12 with jumps.

days.title: Equal intervals
days.work: Fill in missing numbers on number lines counting by 2s, 5s, and 10s.

days.title: Solve on lines
days.work: Solve 8 addition and subtraction problems within 100 on open number lines.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: label 4 number lines and solve 6 problems with number-line jumps.

objectives: Use drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown

days.title: Length stories
days.work: Solve 6 length problems ('A ribbon is 45 cm. 18 cm is cut off. How long is it now?') with drawings and equations.

days.title: Garden fence
days.work: Measure the sides of a small rectangle (table or rug) and add to find the distance around.

days.title: Jump contest
days.work: Measure standing long jumps in inches for family members and write compare problems.

days.title: Two-step lengths
days.work: Solve 4 two-step length problems with number lines.

days.title: Unit 8 test
days.work: Solve 8 length word problems using number lines and equations.

objectives: Determine if a number of objects is odd or even
Write even numbers as sums of equal addends
Find patterns of odd and even

days.title: Pairing
days.work: Pair up counters or socks for numbers 1–20; if every item has a partner, it's even. Record results.

days.title: Equal addends
days.work: Write each even number to 20 as a doubles fact (12 = 6 + 6) and build each with cubes.

days.title: Patterns
days.work: Color evens on a hundreds chart and describe the ones-digit pattern; predict whether 47 and 86 are odd or even.

days.title: Odd + even
days.work: Investigate even + even, odd + odd, and even + odd with 10 examples each; write rules.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: classify 15 numbers or groups as odd/even and write 5 even numbers as equal addends.

objectives: Use repeated addition to find totals

days.title: Equal groups
days.work: Make equal groups of counters (4 groups of 3) and write repeated addition (3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12).

days.title: Arrays at home
days.work: Find arrays at home (egg carton, muffin tin, window panes) and write repeated addition for rows and columns.

days.title: Build arrays
days.work: Build arrays up to 5 × 5 with counters and draw them on grid paper; write two equations for each (by rows and by columns).

days.title: Array stories
days.work: Solve 6 array word problems ('There are 4 rows of chairs with 5 chairs each…').

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write repeated addition for 8 arrays and draw arrays for 4 equations.

weeks.topic: Arrays and repeated addition problem solving

days.title: Tile arrays
days.work: Use square tiles or crackers to build arrays and find totals; record 10 equations.

days.title: Garden plans
days.work: Design a garden with 4 rows of 5 plants and other arrays; write equations and decide if totals are odd or even.

days.title: Same total
days.work: Find all the arrays that make 12 (2 × 6 as 6+6, 3 × 4 as 4+4+4…) using repeated addition.

days.title: Mixed problems
days.work: Solve 6 word problems mixing arrays, equal groups, and odd/even.

days.title: Unit 9 test
days.work: Odd/even and array test (12 items) with drawings and equations.

objectives: Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons by attributes

days.title: Sides and angles
days.work: Sort pattern blocks and cut-out shapes by number of sides and angles; name each group.

days.title: Quadrilaterals
days.work: Explore quadrilaterals (square, rectangle, rhombus, trapezoid) on a geoboard and list what they share.

days.title: Draw to rules
days.work: Draw shapes with given attributes ('a shape with 5 sides,' 'a quadrilateral with no square corners').

days.title: Straw shapes
days.work: Build shapes with straws and connectors or clay; count sides and vertices.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Identify and draw shapes from attribute clues (10 items).

objectives: Partition rectangles into rows and columns of squares

days.title: Cubes
days.work: Examine dice, sugar cubes, and boxes; count faces, edges, and vertices of a cube.

days.title: Shape hunt
days.work: Hunt for 3-D shapes at home and record which have square faces.

days.title: Partition rectangles
days.work: Cover rectangles with square tiles and draw rows and columns; count the total.

days.title: Draw grids
days.work: Partition rectangles into 2 rows of 4, 3 rows of 3, etc. on paper and connect to repeated addition.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: cube attributes and 6 partition-and-count problems.

objectives: Partition circles and rectangles into equal shares
Describe shares using halves, thirds, fourths
Recognize equal shares can look different

days.title: Halves
days.work: Fold paper rectangles and circles into halves different ways; decide which folds make equal shares.

days.title: Thirds and fourths
days.work: Cut play-dough 'pizzas' and paper rectangles into thirds and fourths and label each share.

days.title: Different shapes, same size
days.work: Cut identical squares into fourths in three different ways and explain why each piece is still a fourth.

days.title: Snack shares
days.work: Share a tortilla or sandwich equally among 2, 3, or 4 people and describe the shares ('a third of the tortilla').

days.title: Unit 10 test
days.work: Identify shapes, partition rectangles, and show halves, thirds, fourths (12 items).

objectives: Review addition and subtraction within 100 and 1,000

days.title: Fact fluency
days.work: Take the fluency quiz (40 facts within 20) and compare with the September baseline graph.

days.title: Within 100
days.work: Solve 12 mixed problems within 100 and explain one strategy aloud.

days.title: Within 1,000
days.work: Solve 10 mixed problems within 1,000 using quick pictures where needed.

days.title: Two-step stories
days.work: Solve 4 two-step word problems and write one of your own.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a number-skills self-check (place value, fact families, regrouping) and mark two topics to practice in next week's review stations.

weeks.assessment: Fluency quiz and mixed problem review.

objectives: Review measurement, graphs, money, and time

days.title: Measurement review
days.work: Measure 5 objects in inches and centimeters and solve 2 compare-length problems.

days.title: Money and time
days.work: Count coin sets and tell time at 6 moments today; solve 3 money problems.

days.title: Graph project
days.work: Survey family about favorite summer activity and make a bar graph with 3 questions.

days.title: Shapes and shares
days.work: Draw shapes from clues and partition shapes into equal shares.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Mixed practice set of 15 items across measurement, data, geometry.

days.title: Year-end test part 1
days.work: Number and operations: place value, add/subtract within 100 and 1,000, and word problems.

days.title: Year-end test part 2
days.work: Take part 2 of the year-end test: measure lengths, read a bar graph and line plot, count money, tell time, and identify shapes and equal shares.

days.title: Math fair project
days.work: Plan a 'Math in My Home' poster showing arrays, measurements, money, and a graph from your home.

days.title: Build the poster
days.work: Finish the poster with labeled photos or drawings and practice explaining each math idea aloud in 3 minutes.

days.title: Present & celebrate
days.work: Present the math fair poster to family and review the fluency growth graph from the year.

weeks.assessment: Year-end test and math fair presentation.
